chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abi Usamah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding the mouse, the cat, the chicken, the bird, and the dog, he said: “So long as it has not decomposed, or the taste of the water has not changed, then five buckets will suffice you. But if the water has changed, then its limit is until the odor goes away.”

key_terms.تَغَيَّرَ ٱلْمَاءُ: the water changed in quality due to impurity
key_terms.خَمْسُ دِلَاءٍ: five buckets, the stated amount sufficient in a particular case
key_terms.طَعْمُ ٱلْمَاءِ: the taste of the water, used as an indicator of change
key_terms.يَتَفَسَّخْ: decompose or disintegrate within the water
key_terms.ٱلرِّيحُ: the odor whose disappearance marks the limit mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.ٱلسِّنَّوْرِ: the cat mentioned in the ruling on contaminated water
key_terms.ٱلْفَأْرَةِ: the mouse mentioned as one of the animals affecting the water

ai.seo_question: How should contaminated water be purified if a mouse, cat, bird, chicken, or dog falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on purifying water after contamination by certain animals. It states that if decomposition has not occurred and the water's taste has not changed, removing five buckets is sufficient; but if the water has changed, purification continues until the odor disappears.
